steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: Why is that little girl back again? Isn't that person behind her the one who arrested her last time?

steps.speaker: Pedestrian B
steps.content: She didn't come to wreck more things, did she? I've run out of flowerpots she can smash...

The minute you and OwO return to the neighborhood she wreaked havoc in, you receive many weird looks. But OwO is unbothered by these complaints as she now has her whole mind focused on finding her lion head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It's about this big, this long, this wide...
She gestures animatedly in front of an old woman passing by.

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: I'm sorry, sweetheart, but I have poor vision. I'm afraid I haven't seen the world's most glamorous and beautiful lion head you describe.
OwO doesn't get discouraged and continues to knock on the next door.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I passed by that charcuterie across the street carrying it! I went in for a look, and when I came out, the lion head was already gone.

steps.speaker: Resident
steps.content: No, never seen it! There are too many drooling kids passing by the charcuterie every day. How can I remember every single one of them?
Another door is slammed shut in her face. OwO grimaces indignantly at it.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I-I wasn't drooling! You're the one drooling! Bleh!
Did you ask the charcuterie?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: OwO is not stupid, of course it was the first place I went to. I asked many, many times, but every time, they said they haven't seen it! Then they kicked OwO out.
How is that possible? The lion head is so big and eye-catching. Even if someone had stolen it, they couldn't have stashed it right away. Someone must have seen it...
True, the lion head is so big and eye-catching. Someone must have seen it.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hmm?
OwO tilts her head, holds up her two pigtail buns, and follows the voice.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Who's talking? Like hiding, don't you?!
Hehe, I'm just an old tramp who picks up trash around here...
A hunchbacked old man in ragged clothes strolls out of the hidden bin with a fawning smile on his face.

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Are you looking for the world's most glamorous and beautiful lion head that's about this wide and this big?
The old man simply repeats what OwO just described to someone else, and she immediately falls for it.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Have you seen it? Where is it? Where is it!

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Obviously, that little punk stole it. That kid has no parents to watch over him. He goes around picking pockets every day and survives on help from the neighbors.

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: That dumb kid must have thought that lion head was some rare treasure and nicked it.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: The lion head is indeed a super rare treasure!
OwO argues vehemently, still not realizing the oddness in the old man's words.
This is all just your guess, right? Did you really see him take the lion head?

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Ahaha, why don't you go and see for yourself? That's the only clue you have now. Isn't it better than hovering around here like a headless chicken?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I'm a headless lioness, not a headless chicken!
From what you're saying, you know where this thief is now?

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Of course...
The old man smiles and holds out a hand, palm up, lifting it at you twice.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: What's that? A secret code for the address?
OwO frowns and imitates the old man's gesture, trying to crack the mysterious message in it.
...How much?

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Not much, five hundred.

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Tsk tsk, you don't want to upset this little girl here, do you?
It's pointless to waste more time with someone like him, so you eventually take out five hundred DisCoins. The old man grabs the money with one hand and shows you the way with the other.
You take out the exact amount of DisCoins from your pocket and put the money in the old man's palm. He doesn't hesitate to take the money with one hand and show you the way with the other.

steps.speaker: Old Tramp
steps.content: Ahem. Walk straight to the end and you'll find a hidden alley. That kid likes to hide all his loot in that godforsaken corner.
Counting the cash, the old man staggers back to the end of the street. OwO is still pondering his hand gesture.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: So, what does that gesture even mean? What did you just give him?
Nothing, leave this kind of trivial matter to the clapper. Let's go and have a look at this place he told us about.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Right, the thief. Let's go catch the thief!
You've distracted OwO effortlessly. She now walks triumphantly ahead, while you are still skeptical about this clue you traded with five hundred DisCoins.
Then again, as suspicious as that old man was, he was right about one thing. That boy is the only clue you have now.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I see it! OwO's lion head!
Just as you reach the beginning of the alley, OwO shouts excitedly and jogs deeper into it.
You quickly catch up with her, but are suddenly blocked by OwO who stopped short not far from her destination.
Why stop here? Where's the lion head you saw?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Shhh!
OwO yanks your sleeve to stop you from making any sound. You follow her gaze and see that behind a pile of scrap, OwO's lion head is bobbing up and down rhythmically.
Beneath the lion head is a filthy, short, scrawny body that looks like it's going to get crushed by the head.
The body beneath the lion head is strenuously maneuvering the lion head to squat down and hop up, making tender grunts whenever he exerts himself.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Is he... imitating me?
They're the most basic up and down movements and very poorly attempted, but OwO's eyes can't help chasing the lion head up and down.
That old man didn't lie. It's indeed here...
Normally, OwO would have lunged over yelling "Right! The old man said he's the thief!" But right now, OwO doesn't seem to even hear you.
She focuses entirely on watching the clumsy performance, her eyes brimming with excitement and curiosity.
You don't interrupt her and only peek at the boy's dance with her through the gaps in the scrap.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: One, two, three, four...
Counting the beats softly, OwO seems even more nervous than the lion dancer himself.

When OwO said "imitating me", you thought she meant copying the overall format. But after a while, you realize the boy alters his moves according to a certain pattern. You seem to have seen this choreography before...
This is...?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: This is the performance OwO did in the movie! He's seen OwO's movie!
OwO tries her best to lower her voice but fails to conceal her surprise.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It's coming, the most important final pose!
The small hand clutching your sleeve tightens.
Under your anticipating gaze, the boy tries hard to remember the steps, hops left and right hesitantly, then lifts the lion head over his head toward the sky.
The pose is done. You finally make out the boy's face too. On the small face covered in dirt, a pair of eyes stares at the lion head, glistening with anticipation.
He holds his breath and stays in that pose for five seconds, ten seconds, half a minute...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: What’s he waiting for?
Didn't you choreograph this lion dance? Shouldn't you know?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Oh, but the dance ends here. In the movie, that's the moment when OwO gains the lion head's power and turns into a superhero!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hey, don't tell me you've never watched OwO's lion dance movie! How come you don't know what happens next?
Ahem, of course I have...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Liar!!
The boy suddenly cries out furiously, interrupting your chit-chat.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Nothing happens! It's all just a lie!
Before you can react to the boy's sudden rage, he lifts the lion head high and is about to smash it to the ground...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Ahhh! Stop, you stinking thief!

OwO screams and lunges out almost instinctively. Luckily, with her Mania-enhanced physical abilities and agility gained from years of lion dance practice, she manages to catch the lion head in that precarious moment.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Do you even know what you're doing?! This is the one and only extraordinarily glamorous and beautiful lion head in DisCity!
OwO is covered in dirt from the fall, but she only grabs the lion head and examines it carefully while cursing.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You're lucky it's not damaged. Otherwise, I'm definitely taking you to Goldionville where you'll work your butt off to make me ten lion heads to compensate for my loss!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: You... You're...
The boy seems shocked by OwO's sudden appearance. He looks at OwO, then at you who come out from behind the heaps of scrap, then back at OwO.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: You're that... from the movie...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hehe, at least you're not blind! That's right, I'm the world's number one genius lion dance que...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Liar! You're that big fat liar from the movie!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Huh?!
OwO chokes on the words "Lion Dance Queen," and the anger almost making her jump.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You, you, you! You thief!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Liar!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Stinking thief!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Big fat liar!

The boy may look scrawny, but he speaks with a loud voice. It's the first time OwO has argued with someone even louder and more stubborn than herself. Feeling both anxious and aggrieved, she stomps behind you.
Trapped between two quarreling kids, you feel like your head is close to exploding.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: OwO is not a liar! Waah!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: That's exactly what you are! "Lion dance brings you the power to return home"? It's all crap!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I didn't lie! I did find my way home! Sob... Say something, little clapper!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Then why didn't I find it?!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: I copied what you did, with your lion head! I did the exact same thing! Then why did nothing happen?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: I got nothing! No darn power! No home! No friends! No Mom! No Dad!
The boy yells at you two at the top of his voice.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Liar! Both you and your lion head are just a lie!
OwO seems in shock. Tears still streaming down, she hugs her lion head tightly and stares at the boy blankly with red eyes.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You, you...
She asks, the question punctuated by her uncontrollable whimpers.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You... want... to go home?
Seeing the stupefied OwO, the boy turns his face away in frustration, biting his lip.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Yeah... But I don't know... I can't find it.
When he finishes, he seems to have completely lost the mood to yell at OwO. He slumps beside the pile of scrap and bows his head dejectedly.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I, I'm not a liar! I really do have the lion head's power. I'm very powerful.
Though still teary, she seems to have restored most of her pride. OwO pokes her head out from behind you and takes a tentative step toward the boy, hugging her lion head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I'm... the world number one extraordinarily powerful Lion Dancing Queen OwO!
She pats her own chest with one hand. The boy frowns and stares at OwO, probably guessing what she's getting at.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I'll help you find your home!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: If I could find my home, I must be able to find yours too! Right, little clapper?
Huh? Oh, Yeah!
